doc.title: Rashied Ali and Henry Grimes interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 30, 2009

title: Ali's current quintet and seasonal gigs
summary: Ali on his working quintet since getting an agent and the best months for gigs, especially European festivals.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: And Rashied, I know you’re happy, right now you’ve got your own quartet, is that right?

Quintet actually, yeah. So you know, I have had many quintets since Coltrane’s days, and this is, the one I have now is the most workingist one of all, because the other quartets, the quintets, whatever, trios, that I had since Coltrane, it was just that I was never, you know I’m not really good at hustling gigs on my own. So and I’ve never really had an agent before, maybe since five years ago now. So I’ve never really got a lot of work. So I really couldn’t keep a band together very long without keeping them working. So I went through quite a few bands. But the one I have now since I’ve had an agent for the last five or six years, we’ve been together about four years now. And I’m very happy with it.
What’s a good month for you, as far as your band, as far as gigs?
Yeah. How many times would you play?

I would say in the spring and the fall and the summer months. The winter months aren’t so good. The spring and the fall and the summer months are really good, especially in Europe, because they have a lot of outdoor festivals there and even in America they have a lot of outdoor festivals in the summer and springtime. And so I think most of it’s good — spring, fall, summer is the best times.
